common.target: Supplied target URL. Use localhost for local testing.

environment.dataState: Default demo data in a fresh browser session/context

common.authPrecondition: Unless scenario.public is true, start from a fresh browser session and log in through the UI using the existing browser-local demo account. Self-service signup is unavailable.
knownProductLimitations: The public signing page simulates completion in React state. It confirms validation and a success message only; it does not prove persisted signatures, countersigning, audit trails, or email delivery.

scenarios.title: Anonymous access protection and invalid login
scenarios.goal: Verify protected pages redirect anonymous users and invalid credentials are rejected without creating a session.

expectedOutcomes.description: Opening People anonymously lands on the login page and preserves `/people` as the return path.
Submitting the unknown account shows invalid-credentials feedback.
After the failed login, the user remains unauthenticated on the login page with the same return path.

scenarios.title: Demo login, logout, return-path login, session persistence
scenarios.goal: Verify UI login with an existing demo account creates a session, logout protects routes, login follows return paths, and reload keeps the session.

expectedOutcomes.description: Logging in through the UI reaches the authenticated Sales Pipeline app.
After logout, opening People redirects to login with `/people` preserved.
Logging in with the same demo account returns to People.
Reloading People remains authenticated and still shows the People page.
Logging out again restores People route protection.

scenarios.title: Contact create/edit/delete and reload persistence
scenarios.goal: Verify a contact can be created, found, edited, persisted across reload, deleted with confirmation, and absent after reload without harming seeded contacts.

expectedOutcomes.description: After creating and reloading, searching by the unique email shows exactly one contact with the created name, role, and company.
After editing the role and reloading, the same unique contact shows the edited role.
Deleting the contact requires confirmation or an equivalent destructive-action acknowledgement.
After deletion and reload, searching by the unique email shows the contact is absent.
A seeded contact such as Daniel Ek remains present after deleting the synthetic contact.

scenarios.title: Filtered CSV export and downloaded content
scenarios.goal: Verify filtered People CSV export contains the expected filtered contact and excludes unrelated contacts.

expectedOutcomes.description: The People table filter shows Daniel Ek as the matching contact before export.
Export produces a CSV download artifact.
The CSV has the expected People headers.
The CSV contains Daniel Ek's row and does not contain unrelated contacts such as Sarah Chen.

scenarios.title: Deal creation, drag to Qualified, persistence and table values
scenarios.goal: Verify a new deal can be created in Lead, moved to Qualified using browser input, persists after reload, and appears correctly in the Deals table.
preconditions: Default demo organizations and owners visible

expectedOutcomes.description: After creation and filtering by the unique title, the deal appears in Lead with the supplied company, value, close date, and owner represented in the UI where applicable.
Using genuine browser drag or pointer input moves the deal from Lead to Qualified.
After reload and filtering, the deal remains in Qualified and no duplicate remains in Lead.
In the Deals table, the unique deal shows Spotify, Qualified, $12K, and 30% probability.

scenarios.title: Custom report creation, rendered output, deletion
scenarios.goal: Verify a Pipeline by Stage custom report can be created, reloads with meaningful rendered widgets, and can be deleted without deleting built-in reports.

expectedOutcomes.description: Creating the custom Pipeline by Stage report navigates to a report page with the unique title.
After reload, the unique report title remains visible.
The report renders three meaningful widgets: Deals by Stage, Total Pipeline Value, and Total Deal Count. Each widget must show non-empty numeric/chart data, not just its title.
The report shows an active-deal summary with a numeric active-deal count.
After deleting and reloading Reports, the unique custom report is absent while Pipeline Overview remains present.

scenarios.title: Overdue task, completion and persistence
scenarios.goal: Verify an overdue task appears in Overdue, leaves that filter when completed, and remains completed after reload.
preconditions: Clock fixed to 2026-06-01 UTC when supported, otherwise record the actual UTC date and use yesterday

testData.title: QA Follow Up {run_id}
testData.fallbackDueDate: Yesterday in UTC if clock control is unavailable

expectedOutcomes.description: The create action is disabled until the required task title is provided.
The created task appears under Overdue with To Do status and overdue indication.
Completing the task removes it from the Overdue filter.
After reload, the task remains checked/Done and is not shown as overdue.

scenarios.title: Public signing validation and confirmation
scenarios.goal: Verify the public proposal signing form validates required fields and shows simulated confirmation only after both consents are provided.

expectedOutcomes.description: Submitting empty form shows errors for full name, terms consent, and authorization consent.
Providing name and terms consent alone still shows authorization-consent validation and no success confirmation.
Providing name plus both consents shows the simulated Signed confirmation.

scenarios.title: Actual request headers/body, response and UI feedback
scenarios.goal: Verify the public network test page sends the expected POST request and renders echoed success feedback.
preconditions: Network capture enabled before triggering the request

expectedOutcomes.description: Browser-captured network evidence shows an actual POST to `/api/network-test`.
Captured request evidence includes the expected request ID header, custom test header, and JSON body.
The response is HTTP 200 and echoes the expected header/body values.
The UI shows success feedback and the echoed request ID.
